newsitem.title: UK: Argentina taps into demand for EMU bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentina taps into demand for EMU bonds.

text.p: Argentina launched a 750 billion lire ($438 million) 10-year Eurobond on Friday that will be redenominated into the single European currency after economic and monetary union (EMU).

The bond will be fungible with any future bonds Argentina may issue in currencies likely to become part of EMU. Bankers said the bond was well-received by investors attracted to the high coupon and the deal's EMU clause.
"The deal has captured the interest of a very broad range of investors," an official at lead manager Chase told Reuters.
"Italian retail investors liked the high initial coupon, and because it will be fungible with any future deals, institutions were attracted to its likely liquidity," he said.
The bond pays 10 percent until August 1999, when the coupon steps down to 7.625 percent.
The Chase official said up to 30 percent of the paper had been placed outside Italy.
"Investors like the idea of having a euro-denominated bond by Argentina," he said.
The structure is similar to jumbo lira bonds issued recently by the World Bank and the European Investment Bank, but Argentina's paper pays higher returns.
The World Bank set a 1.0 trillion lire January 2007 bond this week, which pays a 9.3-percent coupon until January 1999, when it steps down to 5.4 percent.
The European Investment Bank has raised 1.5 trillion lire with a February 2007 bond, which pays 9.0 percent and steps down to 5.75 percent in 1999.
International investors have been strong buyers of lira Eurobonds on the back of a sharp rally in Italian debt on increased expectations Italy will join the first round EMU in 1999.
If Italy does not adopt the euro then, the bonds will continue to pay interest in lira.
The spread between German and Italian 10-year government bonds stood at 92 basis points on Friday, down from 150 b.p. a month ago. ($ = 1710 Italian Lire)
